sources.title: Nicholas J. Higham, Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms, 2nd ed., SIAM, 2002
sources.locator: Chapter 24 §§24.1–24.3, printed pp. 451–457; the full chapter and its proof reasoning were read from the complete 710-page text.

contents.name: Theorem 24.1, Cooley–Tukey radix-two factorization
contents.support: Used only as the canonical exact radix-two baseline; the computed proof gives its own rounded stage schedule and constants.

contents.name: Computed twiddle-weight error assumption and Theorem 24.2 forward error analysis
contents.support: The source analyzes a product of perturbed FFT factors and makes twiddle accuracy a separate hypothesis. The local proof derives η=10u+εtw for its explicit six-operation complex butterfly and rounded normalization.

contents.name: Inverse FFT has the same forward-error order under conjugation and scaling
contents.support: Supports the separate inverse-direction claim; the local argument uses the exact conjugation identity and reuses the proven forward bound.

contents.name: FFT-based convolution and a rounding-error question
contents.support: Provides the transform/product/inverse composition context; the item proves a complete local error bound including pointwise products and final scaling.

contents.name: Radix-two base used by the arbitrary-length schedule
contents.support: The arbitrary-length procedure uses the canonical radix-two routine as its power-of-two leaf; the local algorithm specifies its own mixed-radix and Bluestein branches and does not infer their stability from this source.

contents.name: Exact radix-two branch in the arbitrary-length correctness and cost proof
contents.support: The local theorem uses the exact radix-two correctness result for its power-of-two case; mixed-radix and Bluestein correctness and their recursive cost are proved locally.

sources.title: C. Sidney Burrus, Fast Fourier Transforms, Rice University, 2012, CC BY 3.0
sources.locator: Full 248-page open textbook. Read Chapter 5 §5.2 pp. 30–32; Chapter 8 §8.3.2 pp. 76–77; Chapter 11 §11.2 pp. 111–112 and §11.7 pp. 133–135; Chapter 13 §13.1 pp. 139–140.

contents.name: Chirp identity converts a DFT into modulation, convolution, and demodulation
contents.support: The source supplies the chirp-square identity; the local proof establishes residue injection, the M≥2N−1 padding condition, normalization, and exact cyclic-convolution conversion.

contents.name: General Cooley–Tukey factorization for n=n1n2 and mixed-radix interpretation
contents.support: The exact index maps and normalization are restated and proved locally for the assigned unitary DFT convention.

contents.name: DCT/DST as Fourier transforms for finite signal models
contents.support: Used as transform-family context only; the DCT-II and DST-I extension conventions, endpoint normalizations, inverse formulas, and Chebyshev extraction are fixed and proved locally.

contents.name: FFT convolution is cyclic; zero padding prevents aliasing in noncyclic convolution
contents.support: The local proof gives the full index argument for the n+m−1 threshold, including wrapped and zero-tail cases.

contents.name: Logarithmic worst-case FFT error growth requires accurate twiddles; recurrence-generated twiddles can be substantially worse
contents.support: Supports the explicit twiddle-error caveat. The source also warns that some DCT-I/IV implementations have poor error growth; this page claims no finite-precision stability theorem for its DCT-II/DST-I definitions.

contents.name: FFT convolution schedule used inside the arbitrary-length Bluestein branch
contents.support: The local algorithm composes the exact Bluestein chirp reduction with the supported radix-two cyclic-convolution routine; all phase and failure details are stated locally.

contents.name: Exact cyclic-convolution operation used by the arbitrary-length exact-constant model
contents.support: The local proof establishes exactness and the operation-count recurrence; this source supports the FFT-convolution context, while the local argument supplies the complete prime and composite cases.

sources.title: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions, §4.23 Inverse Trigonometric Functions
sources.locator: §4.23(i), equation (4.23.3), general arctangent integral; §4.23(ii), principal inverse-trigonometric branch conventions. Read the complete relevant page sections.

contents.name: Inverse-tangent integral and principal branch convention
contents.support: Confirms the integral representation and principal branch conventions used in the local proof identifying the interval evaluator's arctangent-based pi with the canonical Fourier constant.

pages.source_context: The B page inherits the three full-text treatments recorded for its required A page. Each exact example also cites its specific local or published identity suppliers; the examples make no finite-precision success claim.
